 Judgment
1.

This appeal is filed by the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (for short, 'the
Corporation') of the offending vehicle challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the
Tribunal as exc
essive and seeking reduction of the same and also on negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing registered No.KA-27/H-6513

. 
2. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and respondents.
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the matters are taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their rank referred to in the claim petition before the Tribunal.

4. The Corporation has filed this appeal to modify/set aside the judgment and award in MVC No.1468/2015 date 05.01.2017 on the file of the Additional Senior Civil Judge and A.M.A.C.T.,
Ranebennur.
5.

The brief facts of the claimants case before the Tribunal is as under:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:7808 On 19.06.2015 at about 7.30 P.M. the deceased was proceedings as a pillion rider along with his friends in motorcycle bearing registered No.KA-27/H-6513 as a pillion rider on P.B.road, Davanagere, at that time, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing registered No.KA-17/F-1693 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of the claimant.
Due to the said impact, the deceased sustained fatal injuries to all over the body.

Immediately he was shifted to Shymanuru Shivashankarappa Institute of Medical Sciences Research Centre Hospital, Davangere, (for short, 'the SSIMS'), wherein the injured succumbed to the accidental injuries.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence, claimant No.1 being the elder brother of deceased and claimant No.2 younger brother have filed this petition.
6. Considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.12,19,000/- along with interest at the rate of 7% per annum.
Aggrieved by the judgment and award of the Tribunal the Corporation preferred this appeal, challenging the quantum of compensation as well as negligence.

sentences.text: It is contended that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving on the part of rider of the motorcycle and thus, he has contributed his negligence.
The rider of motorcycle without following the traffic rules take the right direction.
Hence, the accident was occurred.
Therefore, the driver of KRSTC bus and the Corporation are not liable to pay any compensation to the claimants.
Further, the deceased one Shivananda and Shubash were traveling as pillion riders on the motorcycle and one Ramesh, who was riding the motorcycle.
It contravene Section 128 of the M.V.Act.
Hence, the Corporation is not liable to pay compensation.
8. Learned counsel for the claimants submits that the Tribunal considering the oral and documentary evidence available on record, has granted fair and reasonable compensation.

However,
the accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus and hence, the entire liability is saddled upon the Corporation.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the appeal.

In view of the submission made by both counsel and materials available on record, the following points that would arise for Court consideration in this appeal are:
"Whether the Corporation proved that the rider of motorcycle also contributed negligence and hence, Corporation is not liable to pay entire compensation?"
"Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable or does it call for enhancement?"
10.
In order to substantiate the contention of the Corporation, the Corporation got examined Sri.Jnaneshwar Doddamani as RW.1 and relied upon Ex.R.1-payment receipt.

On the other hand,
the claimants examined as PWs.1 to 3 and relied upon Exs.P.1 to 18.

As per the contents of Ex.P.1- FIR, Ex.P.2-complaint, Ex.P.3-Spot Panchanama, Ex.P.6- charge sheet etc., it shows that the driver of KSRTC bus bearing registered No.KA-17/F-1693 came in a rash and negligent manner in order to endanger the human life dashed against the motorcycle and caused the accident.

The oral evidence of PWs.1 to 3 are supported by documentary evidence at Exs.P.1 to P.6.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:7808 11.
Admittedly, the Corporation has not challenged these documents and oral evidence of PWs.1 to 3.
The oral and documentary evidence clearly establishes that, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the KSRTC bus.
Hence, the Corporation is liable to pay the compensation.
12. Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the accident is of the year 2015.
The deceased died bachelor, who was aged about 19 years at the time of accident.

Hence, the future The Managing Director vs Kumar Ningappa Ganter on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93917769/

sentences.text: The claimants have not furnished any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
Hence, the notional income at Rs.8,000/- per month is taken into consideration, which comes to Rs.3,200/-(8,000/- + 40% = 11,200).
The multiplier applicable to his age group is '18'.
Since, the deceased was bachelor at the time of accident hence, 50% income has to be deducted from his personal income.
Therefore, the loss of dependency works out to Rs.12,09,600/- (Rs.8,000/- + 40% X 12 X 18 - 50%) against Rs.12,19,000/- as awarded by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.35,000/- towards 'transportation of dead body and funeral expenses' and Rs.35,000/- towards 'loss of estate' and Rs.15,000/- towards 'love and affection' which is not reasonable one.

14. As per the principles laid down in case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi And Others1, and Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others2, the claimants are entitled for sum of Rs.40,000/- each under the head 'loss of consortium'.
15.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of ratio laid down in case of Pranay Sethi (supra) and Magma (supra), a sum of Rs.15,000/- each is awarded under 'loss of estate' and 'transportation of the dead body and funeral expenses' respectively and the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Hence, the total amount on this head comes to Rs.18,000/- each (Rs.15,000/- +
3000/-).

Thus, the claimants are entitled for the following compensation:
 Loss of dependency Rs.12,09,600/-
 Rs.8,000/- + 40% X 12 X 18 - 50%)
 Loss of consortium Rs.80,000/-
 (40,000 X 2)
 Loss of estate Rs.18,000/-
 Transportation of dead body and funeral Rs.18,000/-
 expenses  Total Rs.13,25,600/-
Less: Compensation awarded by Tribunal Rs.12,19,000/-
Balance Rs.1,06,600/-
17.
Claimants have entitled for total compensation of Rs.13,25,600/- but the claimants have not filed any appeal.
Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on lower side.
Therefore, there is no merit in the contention of the Corporation and hence, appeal is dismissed being devoid of merits.
